messages.author: 661599c031af2f3f
messages.subject: Using variable names within Simulatedata()
parts:
Dear all,
We're working on a tutorial paper that includes Lavaan. One thing we want to do is visualize simulated data and make it really easy to tweak the parameters and see the consequences. Does anyone know an easy way to use variables to define the value of parameters within model specification? So instead of

model1<-'
COGLV=~.8*X1

something like

X1FL<-.8

model1<-'
COGLV=~.X1FL*X1

Two solutions I'm trying to avoid would be 
-using full openmx style matrix notation (as it would be illegible for novices and cumbersome for complex models)
-Some kind of print(paste()) hack that would also be illegible for novices and likely error prone

Any suggestions much appreciated,
Rogier

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Using variable names within Simulatedata()
parts:
On 11/28/2016 10:55 AM, Rogier Kievit wrote:
> Dear all,
> We're working on a tutorial paper that includes Lavaan. One thing we
> want to do is visualize simulated data and make it really easy to tweak
> the parameters and see the consequences. Does anyone know an easy way to
> use variables to define the value of parameters within model
> specification? So instead of
>
> model1<-'
> COGLV=~.8*X1
>
> something like
>
> X1FL<-.8
>
> model1<-'
> COGLV=~.X1FL*X1

In a far future, this might actually work out-of-the box: defining
variables outside the model syntax. But not today.

What I often do myself is this: I create a parameter table, and
manipulate rows/cols in that parameter table. This manipulated parameter
table can be provided as input (instead of the model syntax). For example:

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

# default model
pt1 <- lavaanify(HS.model, auto = TRUE)
fit1 <- cfa(pt1, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)

# fix "textual =~ x5" loading to, say, 0.9:
pt2 <- pt1
idx <- with(pt1, which(lhs == "textual" & op == "=~" & rhs == "x5"))
pt2[idx, "free"] <- 0
pt2[idx, "ustart"] <- 0.9
fit2 <- cfa(pt2, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)

Yves.
